name: proof-tree-companion
description: Editor-side commands for the proof-tree infoview widget: opens a tactic in the lens (a slim editor group split below the infoview) and reveals tree nodes in it, relayed through a request file the widget's Lean RPC writes (the infoview's EditorApi has no executeCommand). Will also grow global settings / persistent state for the widget.

commands.title: Proof Tree: Open Tactic in Lens

proofTree.outlineOnly.markdownDescription: Draw the tree's node boxes as borders with no fill, letting the outline alone carry goal-vs-tactic. Purely how the boxes look — nothing moves and nothing is hidden. A setting rather than a button on the tree's rail because it is a standing preference, not something you reach for while reading a proof.

proofTree.tallFrame.markdownDescription: Let the proof tree run closer to the bottom edge of the infoview. By default it stops a little short, leaving the next section's heading showing — both a reminder that the column continues below and somewhere to put the pointer, since the tree's own scroll container swallows the wheel. Tick this to give most of that strip back to the tree; what remains below it (the restart-file button included) still takes a scroll.

proofTree.linkMarks.markdownDescription: Draw the connectors' target-type marks: a small gapped dot near either end of a line that runs into a goal, a gapped dash where it runs into a tactic — so you can tell what a line terminates at before following it. On by default because shape is the one channel that survives without colour. Untick to leave the connectors plain, which is the right call if you read the target's kind off `#proofTree.linkTint#` or the box shapes and find the marks fussy. Turning this off also suppresses `#proofTree.linkEmoji#`, which only changes what the marks are drawn AS.

proofTree.linkEmoji.markdownDescription: Replace the connectors' subtle target-type marks with emoji: 🎯 where a line runs into a goal, ⚙️ where it runs into a tactic. By default each connector carries a small gapped mark near either end — a dot for goal-bound, a dash for tactic-bound — so you know which kind of node a line terminates at before you follow it; tick this to make the marks unmistakable at the cost of some visual noise.

proofTree.linkTint.markdownDescription: Tint each connector toward the colour of the node it runs INTO (the goals' blue, the tactics' green), on top of the shape marks. Off by default because colour alone is easy to miss and not everyone tells the two hues apart — the shape marks are the baseline; this is reinforcement for those who want it.

proofTree.lensGoals.markdownDescription: Show each tactic's resulting goal inline at the end of its line in the lens, so a proof read there carries its intermediate states. Lens only — the main editor has the infoview for this. The text is drawn as a decoration, so it costs no lines and no width the code was using, and it is dropped as soon as you edit (the widget re-sends it once the file re-elaborates).

proofTree.lensFold.markdownDescription: Collapse everything that is not on the way to the tactic when opening it in the lens, leaving sibling branches as one-line stubs. The lens is only a few lines tall, and what costs it most is the proof around the tactic. Best-effort: how much collapses depends on the folding ranges the Lean server publishes, and with none it simply does nothing.

proofTree.lensWordWrap.markdownDescription: Wrap long lines in the lens, so a slim pane does not spend its width on horizontal scrolling. Applies to the lens editor ALONE — it uses the word-wrap toggle command, not the `#editor.wordWrap#` setting, so nothing leaks to your other editors or windows. Skipped when you already wrap globally.

proofTree.lensShrinkNudges.markdownDescription: How far to shrink the lens below the 50% split it opens at. The split is roughly 8-9 nudges tall, so **lower is taller** — `0` leaves the lens at half the infoview column.

proofTree.counterfactual.markdownDescription: While you are typing a tactic and the proof doesn't elaborate, show the tree **as if the line you are writing were `sorry`** — elaborated in the background — so the tree keeps its full shape, marks where your tactic lands with a dashed stub carrying your draft, and snaps to the real tree the moment your tactic is valid. Costs one background re-elaboration of the current theorem per edited line (cached while you type on it). Untick to fall back to drawing whatever the broken document parses to.

proofTree.typingHoldMs.markdownDescription: How long (in milliseconds) the cursor must sit still after you type before the tree redraws to match the changed proof. While you type in the buffer, each keystroke that gets elaborated is a different — usually broken — proof, and redrawing every one makes the tree shudder; the tree stays locked while the cursor is moving and updates once when you pause. If you already paused, the redraw lands the moment elaboration finishes — this setting adds no delay then. Raise it if you type slowly and still see churn mid-edit; `0` redraws on every change. Edits made *from the tree* (committing a tactic, chips, delete, undo) always redraw immediately, whatever this is set to.
